title: Knowledge check: Comments in R

questions.prompt: For “Comments in R”, which approach best supports a reliable result?
options: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
Trust the first output without inspecting its inputs.
Hide warnings and skip validation to make the result look clean.
Change several unrelated parts at once so the cause of any result is unclear.
questions.answer_key: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
questions.explanation: Comments in R is one step in R Syntax and Fundamental Rules; r is case-sensitive. Assignment creates or replaces objects; expressions evaluate to values even when they are not explicitly printed. Reliable work makes assumptions visible and checks behavior before scaling up.

questions.prompt: When applying “Comments in R” to real work, what should you do before relying on the result?
options: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.
Assume missing and malformed inputs never occur.
Use the same method regardless of data type or the research question.
Remove inconvenient observations without recording the decision.
questions.answer_key: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.
questions.explanation: Run examples line by line and inspect the global environment only as a debugging aid. Record assumptions and known limitations instead of presenting a demonstration as proof.
